# Owned intelligence transport fixture

`owned.bundle` is generated by the actual `intelstore` full-source preparation,
indexing, sealing and USTAR export path using its owned local TLS fixture. It
contains one authored inert OSV-shaped GHSA record, not downloaded advisory data.
Its synthetic timestamps, generation declarations and source receipts are not
publisher authentication, live-feed qualification or freshness authority.

The portable graph includes the applicable GitHub CC-BY-4.0 notice/license text.
The store key, physical root identity and local acquisition MAC are not exported.
Tests import this transport without granting source authority, exercise real
same-executable workers and export/reimport actual files. They do not call OSV.

## Inert explicit-rule matching fixture

`matching.bundle` is a separate authored OSV npm fixture generated by
`TestMatchingFixtureReproducible` in `internal/intelstore/matching_fixture_test.go`.
It reuses `fullSourceFixture` with an in-memory HTTP transport (no sockets/DNS),
and the actual full-source preparation, source receipts, Apache-2.0 OpenSSF
licensing, indexing, sealing and USTAR export pipeline. Standard-library
`testing/synctest` fixes all generation times to `2026-10-02T00:00:00Z`.

All three records affect only `left-pad` version `1.0.0`, with no broad range:

- `MAL-2026-1`: primary active authored malicious-profile example; `2.0.0` is a
  per-record negative, not a global clean verdict.
- `MAL-2026-2`: whole-record withdrawal at `2026-10-02T00:00:00Z`.
- `MAL-2026-3`: unknown `database_specific.withdrawn_versions` correction;
  applicability must remain indeterminate.

Each contains nonempty `database_specific.malicious-packages-origins` with dummy
`packtrace-fixture` source, a lowercase synthetic 64-hex SHA256, and UTC
import/modified timestamps. This is inert source-context test metadata, not real
malware, downloaded intelligence, or registry/publisher authentication. Import
alone is unqualified: operator-designated use requires the independently selected
exact generation, and eligible matching additionally needs the pinned exact npm
origin policy. No manual category/activity override is supplied.

Generation: `dc8bfb195b04f9a352dca3d0aa7f9c609abd67622b8ef261955307645e21aeb4`.
Transport: 119808 bytes; SHA256
`565e9191f9eca0c55b2f7a0dcad08fd30a40d35ce0205e44ea90d3757321af95`.
Local keys/acquisition MACs are not exported.

Normal `go test ./internal/intelstore -run '^TestMatchingFixtureReproducible$'`
regenerates in memory and compares exact bytes, then imports and verifies all
three originals and the operator designation boundary. Generation to disk is
opt-in via `PACKTRACE_MATCHING_FIXTURE_NEW_OUTPUT` pointing at a **new** output
path; the generator uses exclusive creation and refuses every existing file,
including this checked-in fixture. Use the approved cached Go SDK with local
GOTOOLCHAIN and disabled GOPROXY/GOSUMDB; no SDK/download is needed.

## Inert representative-project and correction snapshots

`full.bundle` and `corrected.bundle` are reproducible authored transports from
`TestFullMatchingFixtureReproducible`. They contain503 records for500 package
identities: malicious/OpenSSF source paths, vulnerability/GitHub-reviewed source
paths and strict npm ECOSYSTEM ranges, plus withdrawal/unknown-correction/source
controls. These records and source locations are invented test claims, not real
advisories or downloaded data. No package code is embedded or executed. The real
preparation, source licensing, immutable indexing/sealing and export pipeline is
used with an in-memory transport and fixed standard-library test clock.

- `full.bundle`:1328640 bytes, generation
  `54da5521f1cce480bb34e8930e3167393d000948f1fa2da28b94ce65a945cefd`,
  SHA256 `f520b12b829709f7440a63d581b97341464a265a8428bf2f4b6df6b7fb31b18c`.
- `corrected.bundle`:1330176 bytes, generation
  `a7f46531e25952da50287d31d5170565eb48434728fc978533f3c15ef5609ef7`,
  SHA256 `bbfd8436214a4331f0cdee9e38779d3b86c685f3271b5ccfa0b048b32f13eaa1`.

The second snapshot changes original conditions and withdraws a previously active
record without rewriting the historical generation. Normal tests regenerate and
compare both exact byte streams. `PACKTRACE_FULL_FIXTURES_NEW_DIRECTORY` permits
exclusive creation in a caller-owned new output directory; existing files are
never overwritten. No local key/MAC is included. Source designation, explicit
pinned namespace policy and actual observation qualification remain independent
of fixture import. These checks do not qualify a live feed, every project,
publisher authentication or a native platform.

## First-version-blocker and descriptive-CWE fixture

`explanation.bundle` is authored by `TestExplanationFixtureReproducible` through
the same actual source/seal/export pipeline, using in-memory transport and the
fixed test clock. It contains two inert records: a supported explicit version
plus an unsupported version-string canary, and a separate scoped OpenSSF record
with descriptive CWE objects. No real advisory or package code is copied.

Generation: `bfbaf97ecbb9bf8ca8374c24bcaa817390803cce9e14f4141a9098f9f84e3110`.
Transport:119296 bytes; SHA256
`809df8657e0096497981154a99d8e19373b78ebb4ba1fdfc084585743ab2efcf`.

Normal tests regenerate and compare exact bytes. Exclusive NEW output creation
is opt-in through `PACKTRACE_EXPLANATION_FIXTURE_NEW_OUTPUT`; existing files are
never overwritten. Actual scan tests verify first-reason locators and unchanged
partial-positive/indeterminate behavior without leaking the canary or granting
source authority from import alone. Historical fixtures remain byte-identical.
